description.narrative:
IRC works in some of the worlds most difficult humanitarian crises, supporting people whose lives and livelihoods have been disrupted by conflict, disaster and climate-related shocks. Its overall objective is to help crisis-affected populations survive, recover and regain control over their future.
Through Sidas support, IRC provides life-saving assistance and protection to people affected by humanitarian crises, with a particular focus on those facing the highest levels of vulnerability and risk. The organisation works across a range of sectors, including protection, health and nutrition, education, economic recovery and cash assistance, often combining several forms of support to address interconnected needs.
IRC measures success through improvements in peoples safety, health, well-being, economic security and ability to make decisions about their own lives. Protection, gender equality and accountability to affected populations are integrated throughout its work, with particular attention to women, girls and children who often face heightened risks during crises.
Sidas support enables IRC to respond rapidly to emergencies, maintain operations in hard-to-reach and conflict-affected areas, and adapt programmes as needs evolve. While priorities differ between countries, the overall aim is to save lives, reduce suffering and help affected communities recover with dignity and greater resilience.

Denna insats stödjer International Rescue Committee (IRC) inom ramen för ett flerårigt humanitärt partnerskap 2026–2029, genom en programbaserad ansats (Programme-Based Approach, PBA) för att möjliggöra flexibel och behovsanpassad humanitär respons i konflikt-, katastrof- och klimatdrabbade kontexter.
Syftet med insatsen är att möjliggöra för IRC att leverera snabb, livräddande och skyddsinriktad humanitär hjälp till människor i akuta och långvariga kriser, samtidigt som motståndskraft och återhämtningsförmåga stärks. Stödet omfattar flera landprogram i regioner med omfattande humanitära behov, inklusive Afrika, Mellanöstern, Asien och Östeuropa, samt en mekanism för snabbinsatser (RRM) för plötsliga kriser.
Insatsen omfattar integrerade program inom centrala sektorer såsom hälsa (inklusive psykisk hälsa), skydd (inklusive könsbaserat våld och barnskydd), utbildning i kris samt ekonomisk återhämtning genom kontantstöd och försörjning. Målgrupperna inkluderar särskilt utsatta grupper såsom kvinnor, barn och människor på flykt.
PBA-modellen möjliggör flexibel resursallokering inom landprogrammen baserat på föränderliga behov, vilket stärker effektivitet och snabbhet i genomförandet. Medlen är i huvudsak icke-öronmärkta på landnivå, vilket möjliggör adaptiv programstyrning.
IRC samarbetar med lokala och nationella aktörer genom strukturerade partnerskapssystem som PEERS, vilket bidrar till lokal kapacitetsutveckling och ansvarsutkrävande . Organisationen är verksam i över 40 länder och nådde mer än 36 miljoner människor under 2024 .
Insatsen klassificeras inom humanitärt bistånd med en multisektoriell inriktning och tydligt fokus på skydd, jämställdhet och lokalisering. Förväntade resultat inkluderar förbättrad tillgång till grundläggande tjänster, minskade skyddsrisker samt stärkt motståndskraft hos drabbade populationer.

This contribution supports the International Rescue Committee (IRC) under a multi-year humanitarian partnership for 2026-2029, using a Programme-Based Approach (PBA) to deliver flexible, needs-based assistance in contexts affected by conflict, displacement and climate-related crises.
The objective of the contribution is to enable IRC to provide timely, life-saving and protective humanitarian assistance to populations in acute and protracted crises, while strengthening resilience and recovery capacities. The support covers multiple country programmes across regions with high humanitarian needs, including but not limited to Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Eastern Europe, as well as a Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) to respond to sudden-onset emergencies.
Interventions include integrated programming across key sectors such as health (including mental health), protection (including gender-based violence and child protection), education in emergencies, and economic recovery through cash and livelihoods support. The contribution targets vulnerable groups including women, children, displaced populations and other at-risk communities.
The PBA modality allows IRC the flexibility to program resources within country programs in response to evolving needs, improving the efficiency and timeliness of the response. Funds are largely unearmarked at the country level allowing adaptive programming and reallocation in response to changing humanitarian conditions.
IRC works in partnership with local and national actors through structured systems such as PEERS, ensuring capacity sharing, accountability and localisation of aid delivery . The organisation operates in over 40 countries and reached more than 36 million people in 2024 through humanitarian assistance .
The contribution is coded under humanitarian aid sectors reflecting multi-sectoral emergency response, with a strong focus on protection, gender equality and localisation. Expected results include improved access to essential services, reduced protection risks, and strengthened coping capacities among affected populations.
